claims.quote: A `fact` or `retract` change of `assuming` states rows with `exists` as the form does on its own: `["assuming", ["fact", ["exists", ["?m"], ["and", ["road", "c", "?m"], ["road", "?m", "e"]]]], ["reaches", "a", "e"]]` asks what would hold with a road through a town nobody has named. Each change has its own form's shape, checked as that form checks it, wherever it stands among the changes.

A `fact` or `why` form that holds a `rule` or `invariant` form among its relation calls fails before it evaluates any of them, so it adds no rule: `["fact", ["n", 1], ["rule", ["m", "?x"], ["n", "?x"]]]` fails and the database holds no new rule or fact. `retract` and `assuming` check a rule or invariant form they hold as the form checks itself, in the same order and words.
